status: GitHub application prepared locally; website direction is a contract, not a built or tested website.
story: A curious person who builds useful software and cares about how it feels.

shared.character: Existing V5 moth. Preserve its oversized soft head, compact body, mitten hands, stub feet, unequal antennae and four marked wings. No anatomy change between themes or surfaces.
shared.assets: Reuse brand/animation-v5/character.js and brand/source/applications-v5.js; GitHub uses their static exported PNGs. The website will use the same versioned source and tokens.
shared.palette: UI color roles come from brand/design-system.css. Preserve character cream/green paints from brand/animation-v5/character.js and header grounds from brand/source/applications-v5.js; do not recolor the artwork through UI tokens. Day and night change paint and atmosphere, not proportions.
shared.name: heyNag is the wordmark and personal handle; Nag is the conversational name; Nagarjuna Boddu is the full personal name.
shared.voice: First person, warm, curious, plain and occasionally gently mischievous. Never let mascot dialogue replace useful project explanations.
shared.proof: Use actual work, clear authorship and honest maturity. Private work appears publicly only through owner-cleared case studies.

github.role: An introduction and a small public window into Nag's work.
github.treatment: Static paired headers, universal day avatar, native accessible text and three verified public project links.
github.recognition: The avatar, header moth and heyNag wordmark are intended to make the shared identity recognizable. Immediate recognition and later recall have not been measured with visitors. No essential meaning depends on a tiny gesture or color alone.
github.links: Personal heyNag destinations only. Add heyNag.com only when a useful live destination exists.

website.role: Expand the same introduction into stories of what Nag made, why, the decisions and what happened.
website.firstVisit: Recognizable heyNag wordmark, same moth and palette, clear Nag attribution, real work visible without interacting with the mascot.
website.characterBehavior: Investigate & share: notice a detail, look closer, then invite the visitor to discover it. Warm curiosity is the default; glasses, comic pauses and mischief are occasional expressions.
website.motion: Use the existing expression and gesture rig with interruptible transitions. Reuse design-system.css tokens deliberately; do not stack its older whole-character gesture animations or scale keyframes onto the articulated rig. Static or reduced-motion paths preserve the story. No forced sound or interaction gate.
website.projects: Carry public project names and factual descriptions across consistently. Add richer screenshots, demos and authorized private-work stories when ready.
website.navigation: Link each public story to its GitHub source and link the profile to the site once launched. No automatic redirects or fabricated coming-soon portfolio.

reviewQuestions: Would the avatar, header and future website opening read as the same maker?
Is Nag clearly the author, with the moth acting as a companion?
Does the public sample avoid pretending to represent all of Nag's private work?
Is the identity legible on a narrow phone, in both light and dark?
What is demonstrated now, and what remains a website hypothesis or audience-research question?
